title: Loom & Leaf Storefront
subtitle: Rebuilding a home-goods store so the catalogue loads in a second instead of four.
description: A Laravel and React rebuild of a growing home-goods shop: a faster catalogue, a one-page checkout and an admin the team actually enjoys using.
overview:
Loom & Leaf had outgrown a theme-based shop. Product pages were slow, the checkout spread across four screens, and every catalogue change needed a developer.

I rebuilt the storefront and admin end to end, keeping the existing product data and URLs so search rankings carried over.
problem: Category pages issued a separate query for every product's images, variants and stock, so a page of 24 products made dozens of database round trips. On mobile the catalogue took around four seconds to become usable.
approach: I started from the screens: what each page needs to render, and nothing more. That defined the API responses, which in turn defined the queries.
solution: A Laravel API with eager-loaded, cached catalogue queries, a React storefront that streams the first row of products immediately, and a one-page checkout with address autocomplete.
contributions: Data model and migration from the old platform
Admin panel for products, stock and orders

features.title: One-page checkout
features.description: Address, delivery and payment on a single screen with inline validation.

features.title: Live stock
features.description: Stock levels update without a page reload when an item sells out.

features: Bulk product editing in the admin

decisions.title: Shape queries around the page, not the model
decisions.description: Each storefront endpoint loads exactly the relations its screen renders, in a fixed number of queries regardless of page size.
decisions.tradeoff: More endpoint-specific code instead of one generic product resource.

decisions.title: Keep the old URLs
decisions.description: Products and categories kept their slugs, with redirects for the handful that changed.
decisions.tradeoff: Some awkward legacy slugs live on.

challenges.title: Migrating live orders
challenges.description: Orders kept arriving during the migration, so the final import ran as a short, rehearsed cut-over with a read-only window of a few minutes.

title: Routeboard
subtitle: An operations dashboard for a delivery fleet, built with Laravel, Livewire and Filament.
description: A SaaS dashboard that gives dispatchers one live view of vehicles, drivers and deliveries — replacing three spreadsheets and a group chat.
overview: Dispatchers were coordinating forty vehicles across spreadsheets and chat threads. Routeboard puts deliveries, drivers and exceptions on one screen that updates as things change.
problem: Nobody had a single, current picture of the fleet. Late deliveries were noticed when customers called.
approach: We shipped the smallest useful version — a live delivery board — in five weeks, then added roles, reporting and billing based on how dispatchers actually used it.
solution: A multi-tenant Laravel application with Livewire for live boards and Filament for the back office, backed by MySQL and queued jobs for driver updates.
features: Exception alerts for late or failed drops

title: Ledgerline API
subtitle: A double-entry ledger and payments API where every number has to add up.
description: A backend-only project: a REST API that records payments, refunds and payouts in a double-entry ledger, with idempotent endpoints and full audit history.
overview: Ledgerline is the money layer behind a marketplace: it records every movement of funds as balanced ledger entries and exposes them through a small, strict API.
problem: Balances were stored as single numbers that drifted out of sync with payment-provider records, and reconciling them took a person two days each month.
approach: Model money as immutable, balanced entries instead of mutable balances, and make every write endpoint safe to retry.
solution: A Laravel API over MySQL with double-entry transactions, idempotency keys on every write, and nightly reconciliation against the payment provider.

decisions.title: Immutable ledger entries
decisions.description: Balances are derived from entries, never edited directly. Corrections are new, opposite entries.
decisions.tradeoff: Balance reads need aggregation, so hot balances are cached and rebuilt from entries when in doubt.

decisions.title: Idempotency keys on all writes
decisions.description: Clients send a key with each request; retries return the original result instead of charging twice.
decisions.tradeoff: Every client integration has to generate and store keys.

decisions.title: Integer minor units
decisions.description: All amounts are stored as integers in the smallest currency unit to avoid floating-point drift.

challenges.title: Concurrent writes to the same account
challenges.description: Row-level locks around entry creation, plus a database constraint that rejects any transaction whose entries don't sum to zero.

results: Monthly reconciliation became an automated nightly job
Zero unbalanced transactions since launch (enforced by the database)

title: Kindred Clinic Booking
subtitle: A mobile-first booking MVP, designed in Figma and shipped in six weeks.
description: An appointment-booking MVP for a small clinic group: patients book from their phones, staff manage schedules from a simple dashboard.
overview: Most bookings at the clinic happened by phone call. The MVP lets patients pick a doctor, a time and a reason for visiting in under a minute on their phone.
approach: Designed the booking flow in Figma first and tested it with front-desk staff before writing code.
solution: A React front end on a Laravel API, with SMS reminders and a staff dashboard for managing availability.
